paper.citation: ATLAS Collaboration, Observation of quantum entanglement with top quarks at the ATLAS detector, Nature 633, 542–547 (2024)

phases: the vertex and the Born rule give the lepton distributions and the expected D
D is measured in the threshold window
the separability bound and the measurement are folded through simulation
the observed D lies below the expected one
base: Particle-physics branch (GEN_HEP v1.2) glued to the quantum-information branches

nodes.label: Top quark t (Standard-Model graph, outside its released scope)
nodes.def: Massive spin-½ sector; decays before hadronisation, so its spin is passed to the decay products.
nodes.glue: GEN_HEP v1.2: third generation not in the released graph

nodes.label: Bottom quark b (Standard-Model graph, outside its released scope)
nodes.def: Massive spin-½ sector; enters only through the charged current t̄_L γ^μ b_L.

nodes.label: Spin state ρ(k) of the t t̄ pair (two-qubit state)
nodes.def: ρ = ¼[1 + Σ B+_i σ_i⊗1 + Σ B−_i 1⊗σ_i + Σ C_ij σ_i⊗σ_j] at fixed production kinematics k.

nodes.label: Phase-space ensemble of t t̄ spin states (mass window)
nodes.def: {ρ(k), dμ(k)} for 340 < m_tt̄ < 380 GeV, spins referred to event-dependent axes common to t and t̄.

nodes.label: QCD production of t t̄ (strong sector, outside the released scope)
nodes.def: gg, q q̄ → t t̄; near threshold the gg channel produces a spin-singlet pair.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo model used for folding and calibration
nodes.def: Event generators, parton shower and detector simulation relating parton-level to particle-level quantities.

nodes.label: Charged-lepton direction in the parent rest frame
nodes.def: dΓ/dΩ for t → b ℓ+ ν and t̄ → b̄ ℓ− ν̄ with polarised parent.

nodes.label: Joint lepton distribution (1/σ) dσ/dΩ+ dΩ−
nodes.def: Density of the two charged-lepton directions q̂+, q̂−, each in its parent's rest frame.

nodes.label: cos φ distribution
nodes.def: φ = angle between q̂+ and q̂−; (1/σ) dσ/dcos φ.

nodes.label: Entanglement marker D (entanglement witness)
nodes.def: D = tr C/3 = −3<cos φ>; threshold: separable states have D ≥ −1/3.

nodes.label: Spin entanglement of top-quark pairs
nodes.def: The spin state of the pair is not separable (on a set of kinematic points of positive weight).

nodes.label: Folded separability bound at particle level
nodes.def: Image of D = −1/3 in the fiducial particle-level phase space: −0.322 ± 0.009 (Powheg+Pythia), −0.27 (Powheg+Herwig).

edges.statement: Every two-qubit state is fixed by the 15 Pauli expectation values B+, B−, C.
edges.where: Main, first displayed equation (spin density matrix)
edges.check: exact: the 15 real coefficients (B+, B−, C) are the Pauli expectation values and determine ρ

edges.statement: For t(p_t, s) → b ℓ+ ν through the V−A current: Σ|M|² ∝ (p_b·p_ν)((p_t − m s)·p_ℓ), so dΓ/dΩ ∝ 1 + ŝ·q̂+ in the top rest frame.
edges.where: Main, decay paragraph: the leptons carry the spin information; no derivation and no reference in the paper
edges.scope: general (tree level, massless lepton and neutrino; no on-shell condition is used)
edges.check: exact polynomial identity in all 20 momentum and spin components, m and m_b: Σ|M|² = 8·(p_b·p_ν)·((p_t − m s)·p_ℓ), independent of m_b; in the top rest frame (p_t − m s)·p_ℓ = m E_ℓ (1 + ŝ·q̂): analysing power κ = +1
edges.note: Library facts used and not regenerated: the Feynman rules that turn the vertex into a tree amplitude, and the spin sums Σ u ū = p̸ + m, Σ v v̄ = p̸ − m. The W propagator is a spin-independent factor and is left out. Radiative corrections are not included.

edges.statement: For t̄ → b̄ ℓ− ν̄: Σ|M|² ∝ (p_b̄·p_ν̄)((p_t̄ + m s)·p_ℓ), so dΓ/dΩ ∝ 1 − ŝ·q̂−.
edges.scope: general (tree level, massless lepton and neutrino)
edges.check: exact polynomial identity: Σ|M|² = 8·(p_b̄·p_ν̄)·((p_t̄ + m s)·p_ℓ); in the antitop rest frame (p_t̄ + m s)·p_ℓ = m E_ℓ (1 − ŝ·q̂): analysing power κ = −1

edges.statement: The decays act on the spins as measurements with effects (1 + q̂+·σ)/4π and (1 − q̂−·σ)/4π.
edges.where: not stated in the paper; step of the regeneration of the lepton distribution
edges.check: exact: the unique Hermitian operators with expectation (1 ± ŝ·q̂)/4π on every pure spin state are (1 ± q̂·σ)/4π; they integrate to the identity over the sphere

edges.where: Main, second displayed equation; cited to Ref. [27]
edges.check: exact: tr[ρ (1 + q̂+·σ)⊗(1 − q̂−·σ)] = 1 + B+·q̂+ − B−·q̂− − q̂+·C·q̂− (divide by (4π)² for the density)
edges.note: Uses that the two decays act on different tensor factors, so their effects multiply.

edges.statement: (1/σ) dσ/dcos φ = ½(1 − D cos φ) with D = tr C/3, and <cos φ> = −D/3.
edges.where: Main: D = −3<cos φ>; Methods A.3: linear form; not derived in the paper
edges.check: exact integration: the density of cos φ is (1 − D cos φ)/2 with D = tr C/3 (B+ and B− drop out), it is normalised, and <cos φ> = −D/3

edges.statement: Separable states satisfy tr C ≥ −1, i.e. D ≥ −1/3.
edges.where: Main: tr[C] + 1 < 0 as sufficient condition, Ref. [18]
edges.scope: general (finite mixtures; limits of mixtures by continuity of the linear functional)
edges.check: exact: for Bloch vectors with |a|, |b| ≤ 1 the identity writes 2(1 + a·b) as a sum of non-negative terms, so tr C = a·b ≥ −1 on product states; tr C is linear in ρ, so the bound holds on the convex hull (separable states). Hence D ≥ −1/3

edges.statement: tr C + 1 < 0 iff <Φ+|ρ^{T_B}|Φ+> < 0, which contradicts positivity of the partial transpose.
edges.where: Main: the criterion is attributed to Peres and Horodecki, Refs. [35, 36]
edges.check: exact: tr C + 1 < 0 is the statement <Φ+|ρ^{T_B}|Φ+> < 0, so ρ^{T_B} is not positive and ρ is not separable (partial transposes of separable states are states). Equivalent form: D < −1/3 iff the singlet fraction exceeds 1/2

edges.statement: The bound holds for the phase-space average with event-dependent common spin axes, and a violation implies entanglement of ρ(k) on a set of positive weight.
edges.where: Main, threshold paragraph: statement on averaging over the top-quark directions, Ref. [18]; no proof in the paper
edges.scope: general (two-component mixtures; finite mixtures by induction)
edges.check: exact + SMT: tr C = 2 tr[ρ SWAP] − 1 is unchanged when both spins are referred to rotated common axes, and an average below −1 forces a component below −1

edges.statement: −1 ≤ D ≤ 1/3 for every state; D = −1 for the spin singlet.
edges.check: exact: −3 ≤ tr C ≤ 1, i.e. −1 ≤ D ≤ 1/3 for every state; the value D = −1 is attained only by the singlet (the eigenvalue −3 is non-degenerate)

edges.statement: D < −1/3 implies that the state is entangled.
Near threshold about 80% of t t̄ production comes from a spin-singlet state.
edges.note: Strong-sector dynamics; outside the released graph and not re-derived.

edges.statement: The parton-level bound D = −1/3 corresponds to −0.322 ± 0.009 (Powheg+Pythia) or −0.27 (Powheg+Herwig) at particle level.
edges.where: 1.2 Analysis procedure (second calibration curve); values in 1.3 Results
edges.note: Obtained by reweighting simulated events; depends on the shower model (the two generators differ).
Data, detector calibration and systematic uncertainties; not checkable here.

edges.statement: The observed D lies more than five standard deviations below the folded separability bound.
edges.check: exact arithmetic on the quoted numbers: distance to the folded bound −0.322 is 0.215 = 10.2σ (uncertainties added in quadrature, bound uncertainty 0.009 included); to the alternative bound −0.27 it is 0.267 = 14.0σ; the separation stays above 5σ unless the total uncertainty exceeds 0.043

edges.statement: Observed − expected = −0.067 in the signal region.
edges.where: 1.3 Results gives both values; the difference is not stated in the paper
edges.scope: general (arithmetic only; not a statistical statement of the paper)
edges.check: exact arithmetic: observed − expected = -0.067; this is 2.6σ if the two uncertainties are treated as independent (their correlation is not given in the text used)

edges.statement: The witness presupposes the quantum description of the decay (TQ2–TQ4); it is not a Bell test.
edges.where: the paper does not describe the measurement as a Bell test

operations.note: J_CC gains the term t̄_L γ^μ b_L; by Rule 4 (route composition) this is one more route t(1) ∧ b(1) ∧ W(1) into the same vertex

operations.why: Rule 8 (sector refinement); the released graph omits the third generation and the strong sector
model → observable edges of status 'pred'; TQ2–TQ6 regenerate them from the vertex
D is an entanglement witness in the sense of those nodes: linear in ρ, bounded on the separable set (TQ7)
first shared concept between the particle-physics branch and the two quantum-information branches that is an observable on one side and a state property on the other
Rule 9: these edges carry the fitted and simulated inputs; the conclusion depends on them and they are imports for the kernel

operations.note: observed more negative than expected (TQ16); the paper states that bound-state effects near threshold are not in the generators. A pseudoscalar excess at the t t̄ threshold was later reported by CMS (Rep. Prog. Phys. 88, 087801 (2025))

over the fixed model node (m_cc ∧ m_A) the observables o-cosphi in bins of m_tt̄ form one effect with one witness: an instance of the contraction lemma of the grand network (effect networks are fibres of the historical graph over a model node)
